Threat Scenario: An attacker uses stolen or reused customer credentials to impersonate a legitimate user
Potential Impact: Unauthorized account access and exposure of customer data
Mitigation: MFA; rate limiting; breached-password detection; short-lived sessions

Threat Scenario: An attacker attempts to impersonate an administrator using compromised credentials or session tokens
Potential Impact: Unauthorized privileged access and administrative actions
Mitigation: MFA; phishing-resistant authentication; conditional access; short-lived admin sessions; privileged access monitoring

Threat Scenario: A forged or stolen authentication token is presented to the API as a valid user identity
Potential Impact: Unauthorized API access and account actions
Mitigation: Token signature validation; issuer/audience validation; expiration checks; token rotation

Threat Scenario: An attacker modifies request parameters or form data before submission to manipulate account actions
Potential Impact: Unauthorized changes to account state or business transactions
Mitigation: Server-side validation; authorization checks; integrity controls; reject unexpected parameters

Threat Scenario: A malicious or compromised client uploads altered or weaponized files that are later trusted by backend services
Potential Impact: Malware delivery; document integrity loss; downstream compromise
Mitigation: File type validation; malware scanning; content disarm and reconstruction; object integrity checks; restricted execution

Threat Scenario: An attacker exploits application access or compromised service credentials to modify customer records
Potential Impact: Loss of data integrity; fraudulent account changes; regulatory impact
Mitigation: Least-privilege database permissions; parameterized queries; database auditing; integrity monitoring; service identity protection

Threat Scenario: A user performs a sensitive account action but the system does not record sufficient identity and request context to prove who performed it
Potential Impact: Disputed transactions; weak forensic evidence; inability to investigate incidents
Mitigation: Centralized audit logging; authenticated user and session identifiers; timestamps; request correlation IDs; protected log storage

Threat Scenario: An administrator performs a privileged action and later denies responsibility because administrative activity is not fully attributable
Potential Impact: Loss of accountability; insider threat risk; audit and compliance failures
Mitigation: Immutable privileged audit logs; unique administrator identities; MFA; command and action logging; SIEM alerting

Threat Scenario: An attacker or compromised service alters or deletes logs to conceal malicious activity
Potential Impact: Loss of forensic evidence; delayed detection; inability to reconstruct attack timeline
Mitigation: Append-only or immutable log storage; restricted delete permissions; centralized collection; retention policies; monitoring for log gaps

Threat Scenario: An attacker gains unauthorized read access to customer records through excessive application permissions or compromised service credentials
Potential Impact: Exposure of personal or sensitive customer information
Mitigation: Least-privilege database access; encryption at rest; service identity protection; query monitoring; network restrictions

Threat Scenario: Private customer documents are exposed because storage objects or access policies are incorrectly configured
Potential Impact: Disclosure of confidential documents and possible regulatory impact
Mitigation: Private-by-default storage; scoped access policies; signed short-lived URLs; encryption at rest; access logging

Threat Scenario: Credentials or authentication tokens are exposed through insecure transport handling browser storage or application logging
Potential Impact: Account takeover and unauthorized access
Mitigation: TLS; secure HttpOnly SameSite cookies; avoid logging credentials or tokens; short-lived tokens; secret redaction

Threat Scenario: Sensitive customer data credentials or tokens are unintentionally written to centralized logs and become accessible to users with logging access
Potential Impact: Secondary exposure of sensitive data through monitoring systems
Mitigation: Log minimization; structured redaction; role-based log access; retention controls; sensitive-data detection

Threat Scenario: An attacker sends a high volume of requests or oversized payloads to exhaust frontend resources and degrade availability
Potential Impact: Customer portal slowdown or outage
Mitigation: Rate limiting; request size limits; autoscaling; CDN or reverse proxy protection; health monitoring

Threat Scenario: Automated login attempts or authentication floods consume authentication resources and prevent legitimate users from signing in
Potential Impact: Authentication outage and customer lockout
Mitigation: Rate limiting; progressive delays; bot detection; capacity controls; monitoring and alerting

Threat Scenario: An attacker triggers expensive API operations repeatedly to consume CPU memory or downstream database capacity
Potential Impact: Application degradation; increased infrastructure cost; cascading service failure
Mitigation: Per-user quotas; request throttling; query optimization; circuit breakers; resource monitoring

Threat Scenario: An attacker abuses document upload functionality with excessive file size or upload volume to consume storage or processing capacity
Potential Impact: Storage exhaustion; increased cost; degraded document services
Mitigation: File size limits; upload quotas; asynchronous scanning; storage monitoring; lifecycle controls

Threat Scenario: A normal authenticated user exploits missing or inconsistent authorization checks to access administrative or higher-privilege API functions
Potential Impact: Unauthorized privileged actions and access to restricted data
Mitigation: Centralized authorization checks; role-based access control; deny-by-default permissions; authorization testing; audit logging

Threat Scenario: A compromised administrator account or vulnerable admin function is used to obtain broader privileges than the assigned administrative role permits
Potential Impact: Full administrative compromise; cross-tenant or system-wide impact
Mitigation: Least-privilege admin roles; privileged access management; separation of duties; step-up authentication; privileged action monitoring

Component / Flow: Application API to Customer Database / DF4
Threat Scenario: A compromised application service identity has excessive database permissions that allow an attacker to escalate from application access to unrestricted database control
Potential Impact: Database takeover; unauthorized modification or extraction of customer data
Mitigation: Scoped service identities; separate read/write roles; deny administrative database privileges; credential rotation; database auditing

Component / Flow: Application API to Document Storage / DF5
Threat Scenario: A compromised backend service identity has broad storage permissions that allow access beyond the documents required by the application
Potential Impact: Unauthorized access to or modification of unrelated customer documents
Mitigation: Scoped storage identities; object-level authorization; separate read/write permissions; short-lived credentials; access monitoring
